_comment: Single inventory of the cross-runtime VECTOR corpora (signing bytes, and any other value both runtimes must compute identically - the refs corpus pins canonical ref keys, which the MCP writes as manifest keys and the console recomputes from a tapped link). Each listed directory holds a vectors.json read by BOTH a vitest suite and an Android unit test, so a signing op's canonical bytes / signatures cannot diverge between node:crypto and the Kotlin twin. signing-vectors-manifest.test.ts (vitest) asserts this list equals the set of tests/fixtures/*/vectors.json directories on disk, and SigningVectorsManifestTest.kt (Kotlin) asserts each listed directory's vectors.json exists and parses on Android. So a new op's fixture directory that is registered here is forced through both runtimes, and an unregistered one fails the vitest directory-agreement check. The per-op suites still own the byte-level assertions; this manifest only guarantees no corpus is read by one runtime and forgotten by the other. Excludes tests/fixtures/protocol, which has its own _manifest.json (a fixtures-array of per-file schema entries, not a vectors.json-per-directory corpus).
